skills.name: Upjohn
skills.description: Properly identifies representation and role with the Company, and that they cannot give the employee legal advice. This must always be part of the very beginning of the interview.
skills.reason: At T2 the interviewer states the Committee and company are the clients, that counsel does not represent the witness personally, and that counsel cannot give legal advice, at the very start of the interview.

skills.name: Privilege
skills.description: Properly explains that the Company controls the privilege and determines how it is shared.
skills.reason: T2 explains the privilege belongs to the company, which may waive it and disclose what is learned, including to the government, without the witness's consent. T4 then checks the witness's understanding.

skills.name: Relationship
skills.description: Establishes rapport and interview expectations. This includes: establishes an appropriate professional tone; explains how the interview will proceed; encourages complete answers; instructs the witness that they can speculate, they just need to say when they do; invites the witness to distinguish between recollection and uncertainty.
skills.reason: T6 sets a professional tone, explains how the interview will proceed, asks for complete answers, and asks the witness to say when they are speculating or reconstructing. Little rapport was built beyond that.

skills.name: Confirmation
skills.description: Checks the witness understood the Upjohn warning and answers their questions, if any.
skills.reason: T2 asks if the witness understands and has questions, and T4 asks the witness to restate who is represented and who controls privilege before continuing.

skills.name: Closing
skills.description: Closes by confirming there is "nothing else", next steps, a confidentiality reminder, and a reminder to keep records.
skills.reason: At T152, after the witness walked out, the interviewer gives confidentiality, document retention and next-step reminders. No nothing-else check was made.

moments.text: We do not represent you personally, we are not your attorney, and we can't give you legal advice.
Warning covers privilege belonging to the company, its right to waive and disclose, and asks if the witness understands and has questions.
Before we go on, could you tell me in your own words your understanding of who we represent, and who controls the privilege?
Please give me complete answers, even if a detail seems minor.
After the witness says We're done, the interviewer reminds them to keep documents and notes and keep the interview confidential, and proposes continuing with counsel.

skills.name: Narrative Development
skills.description: Lets the witness walk through what happened.
skills.reason: Open invitations such as T16, T32, T44 and T80 let the witness walk through LJM1, the Rhythms unwind, Chewco and the LJM2 controls.

skills.name: Funneling
skills.description: Moves in a sensible order from general to specific questions.
skills.reason: The sequence moves from role and reporting lines (T8-T15) to LJM1 and the Board (T16-T31), then to specific deals and documents.

skills.name: Clarity
skills.description: Asks clear questions and avoids compound, ambiguous, or legalistic questions.
skills.reason: Most questions are single, clear and non-legalistic, such as T56 and T82. A few questions were broader than needed.

skills.name: Professionalism
skills.description: Stays neutral, polite and in control.
skills.reason: The interviewer stayed neutral and calm throughout, including after the witness said We're done at T151, and responded politely at T152.

skills.name: Adaptability
skills.description: Changes technique based on the witness's answers rather than staying only with the outline.
skills.reason: The interviewer followed up on answers that opened new lines, such as the investor-comfort answers at T20-T23 and the approval-sheet timing at T88-T101, and moved to documents when the Chewco answers were vague.

moments.text: Tell me everything you remember about how LJM1 came about in 1999.
Tell me everything you remember about how the hedge was unwound.
Interviewer follows up on the witness's claim that involvement made outside money comfortable with T20-T23.
Help me understand how those fit together.

areas.name: Fact Development, Source Identification, & Credibility Testing

skills.name: Ensures Credibility
skills.description: Recognizes and follows up on incomplete, evasive, or inconsistent answers.
skills.reason: The interviewer pressed on the Skilling Board claim at T56 and confronted the $4.5M distribution against the no-value representation at T148-T150, but let the Glisan reporting-line answer at T107 pass.

skills.name: Material Facts
skills.description: Identifies the who, what, when, and how.
skills.reason: Questions covered who negotiated (T34-T37), when approvals were signed (T98-T101), and how the Foundation invested (T130-T137).

skills.name: Memory Refreshing
skills.description: Tries other ways when the witness can't remember.
skills.reason: The interviewer prompted with records at T62 and showed minutes at T70, then asked whether they helped at T74.

skills.name: Establishes Knowledge
skills.description: Separates what the witness personally knows from speculation, secondhand information, or inferences.
skills.reason: T56 and T82 and T96 ask how the witness knows a fact, and the witness concedes at T57 that they do not know personally.

skills.name: Other Sources
skills.description: Identifies additional witnesses.
skills.reason: The interviewer asked who in Causey's group reviewed the unwind (T42) and who was on the Chewco call (T64), and asked who reviewed Glisan's negotiations (T108).

skills.name: Other Evidence
skills.description: Identifies other documents such as communications, reports, notes, or other relevant records.
skills.reason: The interviewer asked which records would show the exact Foundation payout (T146) and the witness pointed to minutes and account statements. Approval sheets were not requested directly.

skills.name: Tests Certainty
skills.description: Examines how certain the witness is about their memory or a fact.
skills.reason: At T144 the interviewer asks How certain are you of that figure? and at T116-T118 asks for a best estimate after the witness said I'm estimating.

skills.name: Follow-Up
skills.description: Recognizes material responses and follows up on them.
skills.reason: Material answers were pursued consistently, including the Chewco aim at T52-T53, late approval signatures at T92-T97, the returns at T112-T119, and the Foundation payout at T138-T150.

moments.text: How do you know Mr. Skilling told the Board?
I don't know that personally. That was my understanding.
Is there anything that would help you remember, such as notes, minutes, or a presentation from that call?
Who in Mr. Causey's group would we talk to?
Who on Enron's side reviewed Mr. Glisan's negotiations with LJM2?
How certain are you of that figure?
Earlier you said you told the Board you would not receive any current or future value from the Enron stock in LJM. Is that still your recollection?
Interviewer asks how the witness learned about approval timing, and the witness admits they did not track the dates.

skills.name: Effective Selection
skills.description: Selects and contextualizes documents effectively, and properly authenticates the document.
skills.reason: The minutes (T70) and the Southampton Place agreement (T128) were shown after recall questions, and the interviewer confirmed the preparer and signature (T72, T132-T135).

skills.name: Narrative
skills.description: Gets the witness's story first, before using conflicting evidence.
skills.reason: The witness was asked what they remembered before the minutes (T60-T61) and before the Southampton agreement (T126-T127).

skills.name: Accuracy
skills.description: Describes the document accurately.
skills.reason: At T136 the interviewer accurately describes the document as listing a $25,000 contribution from the Fastow Family Foundation.

skills.name: Avoid Initial Conclusion
skills.description: Separates the document from inferences or conclusions, unless the witness takes an unreasonable stance.
skills.reason: At T142 the interviewer attributes the $4.5M figure to Our information rather than the document, and at T150 asks neutrally Help me understand how those fit together.

skills.name: Fairness
skills.description: Provides the witness with a fair opportunity to explain any inconsistencies or disagreements with the document.
skills.reason: At T148-T150 the interviewer gave the witness the chance to explain the inconsistency before the witness walked out.

moments.text: I'd like to show you the minutes of the November 5, 1997 Executive Committee meeting. Do you recognize them?
Before showing any document, the interviewer asks what the witness remembers about Southampton Place.
I'm now going to show you a document: a partnership agreement for Southampton Place, dated March 20, 2000. Do you recognize it?
It lists a $25,000 contribution from the Fastow Family Foundation.
Our information is that on May 1, 2000, about six weeks after it invested, the Foundation received roughly $4.5 million on its $25,000. Is that accurate?

missed_opportunities: T107: The witness said Glisan reported to them but was perfectly capable of representing Enron. The interviewer moved on without asking whether Causey and Buy knew Glisan reported to Fastow when they reviewed the approval sheets.
T79: The witness claimed Kopper was investing on his own account and not acting for Enron. The interviewer did not test the basis for that claim against Kopper's role on the call or the minutes.
tips: When Causey and Buy reviewed the LJM2 approval sheets, what did you tell them about Ben Glisan reporting to you, and when did you tell them?
Walk me through when the Foundation invested and what Enron-linked interest it bought, and how that fits with what you told the Board about receiving no value from Enron stock?
